2 Respondents 3 and 4 in O.A.No.1980 of 2024 on the file of the Kerala Administrative Tribunal,
Additional Bench, Ernakulam, which was filed by the 1st respondent herein, under Section 19 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, filed this original petition invoking the supervisory jurisdiction of this Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, challenging Ext.P6 interim order dated 09.09.2025 passed by the Tribunal in that original application.

sentences.text: 2. Going by the averments in the original petition, the petitioners-respondents 3 and 4 are aggrieved by the stay granted by the Tribunal against the process of promotion without hearing them.

The original application was one filed by the 1 st respondent- applicant, who was appointed as Food Safety Officer on 06.09.2024, claiming seniority with retrospective effect and consequential promotion.

The petitioners have been working as Food Safety Officers (FSO, for short) since 2013,
and their probation was declared with effect from 2014.
Their promotion is due to the Cadre of Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety.
Two vacancies in that post arose on 30.04.2025.
The petitioners herein 2025:KER:76744 are placed as rank Nos.1 and 2 in the seniority list published by the 3rd respondent.
The Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC, for short) was proposed to be convened on 16.09.2025.
Meanwhile, the 1st respondent herein, who was appointed as FSO only on 06.09.2024 and whose appointment is yet to be notified, filed the original application claiming seniority.
According to the petitioners, the Tribunal, without hearing the petitioners, directed to stay the convening of DPC for effecting promotion of the candidates, including the petitioners herein.

The petitioners contend that the Tribunal ignored the direction of this Court in O.P.(KAT)No.5 of 2025, passed against the previous interim order in the same case, whereby permission was granted to proceed with promotion subject to the result of the outcome of the 1 st respondent's claim.

3. In the original application, the 1 st respondent-applicant has sought the following reliefs;
"1) To direct the 2nd Respondent to consider Annexure-A6 representation and pass appropriate orders thereon modifying Annexure-5 order by implementing the directions in Annexure-A1, Annexure A2 and Annexure A3 judgments /order by giving due promotion to the applicant which arose on vacancies of Food Safety Officer prior to 05.08.2011 and 2025:KER:76744 grant consequential seniority and promotion and the accompanying monetary relief.
2) To direct the 1st Respondent to consider Annexure-A7 appeal representation and pass appropriate orders thereon modifying Annexure-5 order by implementing the directions in Annexure A1, Annexure A2 and Annexure A3 judgments /order by giving due promotion to the applicant which arose on vacancies of Food Safety Officer prior to 05.08.2011 and grant consequential seniority and promotion and the accompanying monetary relief.
3) To direct the respondents 1 and 2 to effect promotion of the applicant in the vacancy on 16.05.2005 in Kasargod Circle or 22.05.2007 in Mavelikkara Circle and include them in Annexure-A10 seniority list by fixing the seniority.

sentences.text: 4) To direct the respondents 1 and 2 to keep in abeyance all further proceedings pursuant to Annexure-A11, till an order of promotion of the applicant to the vacancy of Food Safety Officer prior to 05.08.2011 is issued in compliance of the directions in Annexure-A1 and Annexure-A2 and Annexure- A3 in its letter and spirit.
5) To set aside Annexure-A14 order, G.O(MS) No.1152/2025/H&FW dated 25.04.2025 of the 1 st respondent.

6) To direct the 2nd respondent to appoint the applicant as Food Safety Officer with effect from 16.05.2005 by modifying Annexure-A5 order and include him in the Seniority List of Food Safety Officers and grant further promotions".
4. When the original application came up for consideration 2025:KER:76744 before the Tribunal,
along with O.A.Nos.26 of 2025 and 56 of 2025, the Tribunal passed the impugned interim order,
which reads thus;
"In spite of repeated postings, the 1 st and 2nd respondents have not filed reply statements.

The learned counsel for the applicants submits that the official respondents are proposing to hold Departmental Promotion Committee [DPC] and effect promotion to the post of Assistant Commissioner, Food Safety without considering the claim of the applicants.
2. The learned Government Pleader seeks time to file reply statement of respondents 1 and 2.
Respondents 3 & 4 in O.A.No.1980 of 2024 seeks time for filing reply statement.
3. Post after three weeks (06.10.2025) for the reply statement of the respective respondents.
Till such time, DPC for promotion to the post of Assistant Commissioner, Food Safety shall not be held."

5. On 15.09.2025, when this original petition came up for consideration, after considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners-respondents 3 and 4, the learned counsel for the 1st respondent-applicant and the learned Senior Government Pleader for respondents 2 and 3, we granted interim stay of the operation of Ext.P6 order dated 09.09.2025.

It was further ordered that promotions, if any, effected to the post of Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety shall be subject to the 2025:KER:76744 final outcome of the original application as ordered in Ext.P5 order dated 21.07.2025.
6.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners-respondents 3 and 4, the learned counsel for the 1 st respondent-applicant and the learned Senior Government Pleader for respondents 2 and 3.
7.
Ext.P6 interim order dated 09.09.2025 passed by the Tribunal is one modifying Ext.P5, the previous interim order dated 21.07.2025 passed by the Tribunal.

By Ext.P5, the Tribunal ordered that the promotions, if any, effected to the post of Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety will be Indu V.S vs Saran G on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17427968/
4
subject to the result of that original application
. By Ext.P6 order dated 09.09.2025, the Tribunal modified the said interim order and allowed respondents 2 and 3 herein to file reply statements within three weeks.

8. The grievance of the petitioners during the hearing is that the Government is not filing the reply statements in spite of repeated directions by the Tribunal, and thus prolonging the decision on merits to be taken by the Tribunal.
The learned counsel further submitted that the matter is now posted before the Tribunal on 21.10.2025.

In such circumstances, we are of the opinion that the Tribunal can be directed to consider the matter on merits and dispose of the same after giving the parties an 2025:KER:76744 opportunity to put forward their contentions.

In the result, without expressing anything on the factual and legal contentions raised by the parties,
this original petition is disposed of, directing respondents 2 and 3 herein to file their reply statements before the Tribunal within three weeks, if not already filed, and the further extension for filing the reply statements will be granted by the Tribunal only on exceptional reasons.

The parties are at liberty to approach the Tribunal with a petition for an early hearing, and on completion of the pleadings, the Tribunal shall decide the matter on merits as expeditiously as possible, taking into consideration the urgency pointed out by the petitioners.
